what: The heuristic precomputes customer/depot fact handles, demands, capacity and vehicle limits (when available), and directed direct/via-depot routing costs from grounded operator names and metric operator costs. At evaluation it reads the current location, visited set, load and vehicle count, then greedily extends the current route: among unvisited customers it chooses the cheapest feasible direct `visit` or, from a customer, `visit-via-depot`, respecting capacity and vehicles, and finally adds the return-to-depot cost. This constructs a concrete remaining plan whose cost is returned as h.
why: CVRP instances expose their routing costs through grounded `visit`, `visit-via-depot`, and `return-to-depot` operators. A nearest-neighbor completion is cheap, requires no complex optimization at evaluation, and gives a state-specific upper bound that is much tighter than static lower bounds. It uses exact-name lookups only for optional capacity/demand/max_vehicles, and it degrades gracefully if those numeric fluents are folded by the translator.
